title: A Rewraps language
description: One file per language under languages/. The build validates it and generates the table the engine matches on, so a new language costs data, not code. Run `cargo xtask new-language <name>` to start one.

name.description: Display name, also matched against the editor's language id when it has no separate id.

id.description: Editor language id, when it differs from the name lowercased without spaces.

ext.description: File extensions ('.rs') or exact file names ('Makefile'). Used when the editor reports no language id, or a generic one.

notes.description: Why this language is shaped the way it is. Shown by `cargo xtask coverage`; never parsed.

comments.description: Every way this language writes a comment. The engine picks the longest matching marker, so order does not matter; a duplicate marker is a build error.

kind.description: line: a marker repeated on each line. delimited: a start and end marker. string: a quoted documentation string.

line.description: For kind=line: the marker, exactly as written, e.g. '//' or '# '.

nesting.description: Whether opening markers nest inside one another (Rust '/* */', OCaml '(* *)').

decorate.description: The character a block-comment body line conventionally carries before its text, e.g. '*' for '/* * text */'. Re-emitted on every new line.

dialect.description: How the text inside this comment is read. A new dialect is the expensive axis; reuse an existing one.

single_line.description: For kind=string only, and required: whether a string that opens and closes on the same line may be split. 'skip' is the safe default, because a newline inside a literal changes its value.

not_followed_by.description: Reject this marker when the next character is this one. Used for '#!' shebangs, which are not comments.

notes.description: Why this shape is here. Never parsed.
